{{Short description|Spanish mathematician}}
{{BLP sources|date=May 2010}}

'''David Ríos Insua''' (born June 21, 1964 in [[Madrid]]) is a [[Spanish people|Spanish]] [[mathematician]], and son and disciple of [[Sixto Ríos]], the "father of Spanish statistics." He is currently also the youngest Fellow of the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]] (de la Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales, RAC),<ref>{{Citation
|url          = http://www.rac.es/2/2_ficha.php?id=161&idN3=6&idN4=40
|title          = David Ríos Insua, RAC Fellow
|accessdate          = October 9, 2009
|author          = Royal Academy of Sciences, Spain
|year          = 2009
|archive-date          = March 6, 2013
|archive-url          = https://web.archive.org/web/20130306134627/http://www.rac.es/2/2_ficha.php?id=161&idN3=6&idN4=40
|url-status          = dead
}}</ref> which he joined in 2008.<ref>Anuario de la Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales. Anuario 2009.</ref><ref>Anuario del Instituto de España. Anuario 2009.</ref> He received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Computational Sciences at the [[University of Leeds]]. He is Full Professor of the Statistics and Operations Research Department at [[Rey Juan Carlos University]] (URJC),<ref>
{{Citation
|url          = http://www.urjc.es
|title       = David Ríos Insua, Full Professor at URJC
|accessdate=October 26, 2009
|author        = Rey Juan Carlos University
|year          = 2009
}}
</ref> and he has been Vice-dean of New Technologies and International Relationships at URJC (2002–2009). He has worked in fields such as [[Bayesian inference]] in neuronal networks, MCMC methods in decision analysis, Bayesian robustness or adversarial risk analysis. He has also worked in applied areas such as Electronic Democracy,<ref>
{{Citation
|url          = http://www.madridiario.es/2009/Enero/ciencia-tecnologia/noticias/124553/entrevista-rios-e-democracia-ciencia.html
|title       = David Ríos Insua, Interview about Electronic Democracy in Madridiario
|accessdate=October 26, 2009
|author        = Madridiario
|year          = 2009
}}
</ref> reservoirs management, counterterrorism model and many others. He is married and has two daughters.

==Career==
* He obtained his master's degree in Mathematics at [[Universidad Complutense de Madrid]] (UCM, 1987), with Extraordinary and National Awards.
* He did his PhD studies at Manchester and Leeds where he obtained his PhD degree in 1990.
* He has been a lecturer and researcher at [[Universidad Politécnica de Madrid]] (UPM), [[Duke University]], [[Purdue University]], [[Université Paris-Dauphine]], [[International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis]] (IIASA), Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche-Istituto di Matematica Applicata e Tecnologie Informatiche (CNR-IMATI),<ref>
{{Citation
|url          = http://www.imati.cnr.it/
|title       = Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche-Istituto di Matematica Applicata e Tecnologie Informatiche
|accessdate=October 26, 2009
|author        = Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche, Italia
|year          = 2009
}}
</ref> Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute (SAMSI), where he was director of the Risk Analysis, Extreme Events and Decision Theory program.<ref>
{{Citation
 |url         = http://www.samsi.info/programs/2007riskanalysisprogram.shtml
 |title       = 2007-08 Program on Risk Analysis, Extreme Events and Decision Theory
 |accessdate  = October 26, 2009
 |author      = Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute, US
 |year        = 2009
 |url-status     = dead
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20100220070239/http://www.samsi.info/programs/2007riskanalysisprogram.shtml
 |archivedate = February 20, 2010
}}
</ref>
* He was director of the Towards Electronic Democracy (TED) program de la European Science Foundation (ESF).<ref>{{Citation
 |url          = http://www.esf.org/index.php?id=2341
 |title        = Towards Electronic Democracy: Internet based complex decision support (TED)
 |accessdate   = October 26, 2009
 |author       = European Science Foundation
 |year         = 2009
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20110927085449/http://www.esf.org/index.php?id=2341
 |archive-date = 2011-09-27
 |url-status     = dead
}}</ref>
* He is current codirector of the Algorithmic Decision Theory (ALGODEC) program<ref>{{Citation
|url          = http://cost-ic0602.org/
|title       = Algorithmic Decision Theory (ALGODEC)
|accessdate=October 26, 2009
|author        = COST-ESF
|year          = 2009
}}
</ref> cofunded by the European Cooperation in Science and Technology (COST) and the European Science Foundation (ESF).
* He has supervised 15 PhD theses.
* He has supervised over 40 cofunded projects.

==Awards==
* Extraordinary and National master's degree Award.
* UPM Award for young researchers.
* Ramiro Melendreras Award of Sociedad de Estadística e Investigación Operativa (SEIO) for young researchers.<ref>
{{Citation
|url          = http://www.seio.es/
|title       = Premio Ramiro Melendreras de la SEIO para David Ríos Insua
|accessdate=October 26, 2009
|author        = Sociedad de Estadística e Investigación Operativa
|year          = 2009
}}
</ref>
* Peccei Award from International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA) for young researchers.
* WirsboURJC Research Award.
* [[Everis]] Award from Capital Semilla.
* SRA Award for best Decision Analysis paper.
